about: What fails around the code: the tools, the services, the tests and the pipeline. Each row says how to recognise the failure, its cause and the next step. `family` is the kind the diagnoser gives it: transient, environment, code, test or spec.

rows.title: Failure: `nuclear`, `nuclear-mcp` or `nuclear-builder`: command not found
rows.summary: The tool is not installed, or it is not on the PATH of the program that ran it (an editor started from the desktop does not have `~/.local/bin`). Install with the installer or `installer/install.sh`, and check with `nuclear doctor`.
body: **Looks like.** `nuclear: command not found`, `nuclear is not installed (run the NuclearLang installer)`, exit code 127.
**Cause.** The binaries live in `~/.local/bin`. A terminal has that folder on its PATH; a desktop program may not.

**Next step.** `which nuclear synapsis nuclear-builder`; install (`curl -fsSL https://nuclearlang.github.io/install.sh | sh`, or `./install.sh` in the source tree); add `~/.local/bin` to the PATH; `nuclear doctor` lists what else is missing. The Builder adds the installers' folders by itself.
asks: the terminal says synapsis is not a command

rows.title: Failure: the installed tools are older than the source tree
rows.summary: A command, a kind or a diagnostic that exists in the sources is unknown to the installed binary, or the editor reports an error the terminal does not: the installed copy is stale. Run `installer/install.sh` again after changing the compiler, a dialect or the CLI.
body: **Looks like.** `nuclear: unknown command`, a kind the docs describe is `N0201`, the editor and `nuclear check` disagree, a Python package of a folder dependency behaves like an old version.
**Cause.** `nuclear`, the language server and the editors' bundled copies are installed copies; a project's folder dependency is installed into its `build/.venv`.

**Next step.** `installer/install.sh` (it rebuilds and reinstalls everything); in a project, a folder dependency is not reinstalled by `nuclear install` once installed: `build/.venv/bin/pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps <the folder>` ; in a web project, delete `build/app/node_modules/synapsis-web` and run `nuclear install` again (the CLI's roadmap). Restart the editor to load the new server.

rows.title: Failure: the Nuclear Smart Graph is not reachable
rows.summary: A search, an ingest or an agent's recall cannot connect to `127.0.0.1:7878`: the graph's server is not running. Start its service again (`nuclear-builder setup --status` says what is down); an agent that cannot reach it goes on without knowledge and says so in its trace.
body: **Looks like.** `the graph is not running at http://127.0.0.1:7878: start it with nuclear-graph serve`, `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:7878`, `connection refused`.

**Cause.** `nuclear-graph serve` is not running, or it listens on another port (`NUCLEAR_GRAPH_PORT`, `NUCLEAR_GRAPH_URL`). Its embeddings model is its own (EmbeddingGemma in ONNX, `nuclear-graph model` downloads it): no Ollama.

**Next step.** `nuclear-builder setup --status`; then restart the service: `systemctl --user restart nuclear-graph` on Linux, `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/io.github.nuclearlang.graph` on macOS, or the button of VS Code's *Settings and integrations* (`Ctrl+Alt+S`). A machine set up by the installer starts it at every login; one never set up: `nuclear-builder setup`. By hand: `nuclear-graph serve &`. Then `nuclear-graph stats` (the rows of each shelf and the revision).

rows.title: Failure: a program has no access to the graph (401, 403)
rows.summary: The graph answers 401 (no token) or 403 (the token lacks a scope): no program reads it until you allow it. Give the client access with `nuclear-graph connect <client> --scopes read,write`, or allow its pending request.
body: **Looks like.** `'mcp' has no access to the Nuclear Smart Graph`, `401`, `a token is needed: ask for access (POST /v1/access) and let the user allow it`, `403` (the token lacks a scope).
**Cause.** Each client has its own token, kept in your keyring, with scopes: `read` (search, cards, prompts), `write` (remember, add examples), `admin` (ingest, manage: only the owner).

**Next step.** `nuclear-graph connect mcp --scopes read,write` (the MCP server), with the graph running; `nuclear-graph requests` shows who asked; `nuclear-graph allow <request>`. Restart the client so it reads its token (`NUCLEAR_GRAPH_TOKEN`, else the keyring).
**The keyring was closed.** A graph that starts at login may run before the keyring opens: it waits for the keyring, then refuses, and never makes a second key or token.

rows.title: Failure: the Nuclear Developer is not running (it is on standby)
rows.summary: The Nuclear Developer (the local agents at `127.0.0.1:7879`) is on standby (ADR-platform-0013): no set-up installs it and no team, MCP tool or chat uses it. A message that it is not running comes from an installation before that decision or a team member of the old local kind: update NuclearLang (`nuclear update`) and give the work to an agent or an API provider.
body: **Looks like.** `the local developer is not running at http://127.0.0.1:7879`, `fetch failed`, a run that stops at its preflight step naming the Developer.
**Cause.** An installation from before ADR-platform-0013, or a team member of the kind `local`. The local models are off behind one switch: `localModels: false` in Nuclear Builder's `setup.json`.

**Next step.** `nuclear update` (or the installer again): the set-up runs the profile `remote`, takes away the Developer's service, the models NuclearLang pulled and Ollama when NuclearLang installed it, and says the GB freed. A team member of the old local kind is converted on read to the default external choice (the first agent whose command is on the PATH: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build; else an API provider with a key in the vault), the team's old file kept as `<id>.json.bak` and a warning shown. Then `nuclear-builder retry <run>`: the steps that passed are kept.

rows.title: Failure: the set-up stops because a service started by hand answers on its port
rows.summary: The set-up of the AI services stops at *Start the Smart Graph* (or *Nuclear Chat*) with `a ... started by hand already answers at ...`: a graph or a chat service started in a terminal holds the port, so the system's service cannot take it. Stop that process with the command the message gives and try the step again.
body: **Looks like.** `a Nuclear Smart Graph started by hand already answers at http://127.0.0.1:7878/v1/health: stop it (pkill -f 'nuclear-graph serve') and run the set-up again, so the service of this system takes its place`.

**Cause.** Before the set-up existed the services were started with `nuclear-graph serve &` and `nuclear-chat serve &`. Such a process keeps running old code and is gone after a restart of the machine; the set-up does not kill a process it did not start.

**Next step.** `pkill -f 'nuclear-graph serve'` (the graph) or `pkill -f 'nuclear-chat serve'` (Nuclear Chat); then *Try again* in the wizard, or `nuclear-builder setup --profile remote --yes`. A service the editor started (the settings page's *Start*) stops when the editor closes.

rows.title: Failure: Ollama is not running, or a model is not installed
rows.summary: NuclearLang's own local models (Ollama, the Nuclear Developer) are on standby (ADR-platform-0013): no tool of NuclearLang needs Ollama or a pulled model, and the Smart Graph runs its own model. Such a message from NuclearLang's tools comes from an old installation: update it. An app of yours with the `ollama` plugin needs Ollama running with its model pulled.
body: **Looks like.** `model 'qwen2.5-coder:3b' not found`, `the Nuclear Developer does not answer at ...`, `connection refused` on port 11434 (`OLLAMA_URL`, default `http://localhost:11434`).

**From NuclearLang's tools.** `nuclear update` (or the installer again): the set-up runs only the profile `remote` and takes away what NuclearLang put there for the local models (the Developer, the models it pulled, Ollama when it installed it; what was on the machine before stays). The work goes to the agents and API providers you choose (`faq:local-models`).
**From your app** (a backend with `plugins(ollama = true)`): start Ollama (`ollama serve`) and pull the model its connection names (`ollama pull <model>`; `ollama list` shows what is installed).

rows.title: Failure: a call timed out, or answered 429, 502, 503 or 504
rows.summary: A service was busy or starting. It is a passing failure: the caller retries it with growing waits (five tries by default). When it keeps failing, the service it names is down: start it.
body: **Looks like.** `timed out`, `timeout`, `temporarily unavailable`, a status 408, 425, 429, 502, 503 or 504.

**Next step.** Nothing at first: the Builder retries with exponential backoff (`.nuclear/builder.json`, `retry`). Still failing: see which service the message names (the graph, Nuclear Chat, an agent or an API provider) and start it; then `nuclear-builder retry <run>`. A compiler error or a failing test is never retried blindly.

rows.title: Failure: the folder is not a Synapsis project
rows.summary: A project command of `nuclear` (`build`, `run`, `test`, `gen`...) or `nuclear-builder` finds no `config.nuc` (or `main.nuc`) in the folder or above it. Run it inside a project, or create one with `nuclear new <name> -p <platform>`.
body: **Looks like.** `no main.nuc or config.nuc in <folder> or above`, `<folder> is not inside a Synapsis project (no config.nuc)`.
**Next step.** `cd` into the project (the folder that has `config.nuc`), or `--project <dir>`; a new one: `nuclear new <name> -p backend|mobile|web`.

In a workspace's root (`.workspace/workspace.nuc`, not a project itself), `nuclear check` checks every app of the workspace; a command that needs one project is run in that app's folder (`nuclear workspace show` lists them) (concept:workspace).

rows.title: Failure: a package of the generated project is missing
rows.summary: The build ran but the runtime or a package was never installed, or a plugin was enabled after the last install: `ModuleNotFoundError`, `Cannot find module`. Run `nuclear install` (and `nuclear build` first when `config.nuc` changed).
body: **Looks like.** `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named ...`, `Cannot find module ...`, `No such file or directory: .venv`.
**Cause.** `build/` carries only the packages of the enabled plugins; they are installed by `nuclear install`, not by the build.

**Next step.** `nuclear build && nuclear install`. For a mobile app that does not build after many changes: `nuclear repair`. Never install a package by hand inside `build/`: add it in `config.nuc` (`plugins(...)`, `dependencies(...)`).

rows.title: Failure: a test fails
rows.summary: `nuclear test` reports a failed test. Read it at its `.nuc` lines with `nuclear explain`, decide whether the code or the test is wrong, fix that file and run again. A test is never deleted or weakened to pass.
body: **Looks like.** `FAILED`, `AssertionError`, `1 failed`, `tests failed`.
**Most common causes.**
- The test reads rows it never created: the database starts empty in every test.
- The code answers another status or value than the criterion says.
- The test kept a `Result` and compared it with a value (`found == 1` instead of `found.value == 1`).
- A call without `~`.
**Next step.** `playbook:fix-a-failing-test`. In the Builder this is the *Verification* stage: three rounds, then the diagnoser explains what is left.

rows.title: Failure: the plan has no pieces
rows.summary: The local planner could not split the spec: it names nothing to build in the platform's words. Name every piece in the spec (a model `Character`, a repository `CharacterRepository`, a use case `ListCharacters`, an appcomponent, a controller), or let a frontier model lead, then restart from the plan.
body: **Looks like.** `0 pieces`, `no pieces`, `the plan does not cover the spec`.
**Cause.** A spec in plain words ("an author has a name; POST /authors adds one") needs someone to decide the names and the files; the local planner splits what a spec says, it does not design.

**Next step.** One sentence per declaration, with its kind word and its name; or give the resource's data (a `GET <url>` line, an example answer) so the generators write it; or give the station to a team member worked by a stronger agent or model. Then `nuclear-builder retry <run> --from plan`.
keys: plan does not cover the spec

rows.title: Failure: a test or a piece uses a class that is not in the plan
rows.summary: The compiler reports `N0220` for a class of the project that no file declares, and the plan never had it: the plan does not cover the spec. Repairing the file goes in circles; the plan needs the missing piece.
body: **Looks like.** `N0220 'CharactersAppComponent'` on an `inject<...>()`, together with `X is not in the plan`.
**Cause.** The planner made fewer pieces than the feature needs (one entity for a spec that needs a facade and a use case), or the tester copied an example with classes of another project.
**Next step.** Name the missing declaration in the spec, or let a frontier model plan; restart from the plan. It is a failure of the spec, not of the code.

rows.title: Failure: `nuclear gen` refuses to write
rows.summary: Before writing anything a generator refuses: a field type nobody declared, a name another file already declares, a source the platform has no pieces for, or a use case to wire that the project does not declare. It says which; nothing was written.
body: **Looks like.** `Character is already declared in <file>: remove or rename it, or generate another name`, `the type Origin is not declared`, `a database resource takes columns of basic types; a relation to Author is written by hand`.
**Next step.**
- A name already declared: the resource exists (`nuclear gen inspect`); use it, choose another name, or remove the leftover file of an earlier attempt.
- A type not declared: generate that model first, or let `--from-json` find the nested models.
- A relation in a database resource: generate the resource with its basic columns, then add the relation by hand (`@manyToOne` and its `<name>Id` column).
- A source the platform lacks: mobile and web read APIs (`--source rest`); a database resource is for the backend.

- `<Name> is not declared` (`gen usecase`): write the use case first, at the place the message gives, then run the command again to wire it; or pass `--calls <Repository>.<method>` when all it does is call a repository.
- `the route names {x}, which the use case does not take`: a `{name}` of `--route` must be a parameter of the use case's `exec`.
- `the <platform> platform has no routes`: `--route` is for the backend; on mobile and web a screen calls the facade's alias.
- See first what it would write: `--dry-run`.

rows.title: Failure: the target's analyzer rejects the generated code
rows.summary: `nuclear check` reports nothing but the target's analyzer or the run complains inside `build/`. Never fix it there. The usual cause is a value without a type in the `.nuc`; otherwise it is a bug of the dialect to report.
body: **Looks like.** An error whose file is under `build/`, from the target's analyzer or at run time.

**Next step.** `nuclear explain` gives the `.nuc` lines. Declare the type of the value at that line (`items: string[] = ...`); check that the call is awaited; rebuild. Still wrong with correct Nuclear: it is the dialect's bug; report the `.nuc` and the generated lines.

rows.title: Failure: the API answers 400, 404 or 409
rows.summary: A backend written in Nuclear answers the status of its `Result` error: 400 an invalid body (a model's rule: the reasons) or `Invalid`, 401 `Unauthorized`, 403 `Forbidden`, 404 `NotFound`, 409 `Conflict`. It is the code working: send a valid request or expect that status in the test.
body: - 400: a field breaks a rule decorator of the model (`@minLength`, `@email`...), or its value is of another JSON type than the field's (`"30"` for an `int`: rule `type`). The answer names the field.
- 400 rule `type` on an exact field: a `bigint`/`bigdouble` is sent as a JSON text (`"0.3"`), never a number.
- 404: `find(id)` or `getOne()` found no row and the use case returned `NotFound`.

- 409: the use case returned `Conflict` (a repeated unique value), or the database refused the write for integrity (unique, foreign key, a null in a required column, a text longer than its column): `message` is `conflict`.
In a test: `expect(found.error.status == 404)`.

rows.title: Failure: no space left on the device
rows.summary: A run, a build or the evaluation stops because the temporary folder or the disk is full. Builds of example projects and Flutter leave large temporary folders: free the space and retry from the failed step.
body: **Looks like.** `No space left on device`, a run whose files are cut short; or a run that stops at its first step, *Check the connections*, with `278 MB free in /tmp (at least 500 MB are needed: free some space there)`: the message names the folder that is full (the project's, or the temporary one, which on many systems is memory with a size of its own).

**Next step.** `df -h /tmp ~`; remove scratch projects and old temporary build folders (`flutter_tools.*`, `nuclear-lsp-*`, `nuclear-web-device-*` in the temporary folder); `nuclear-builder retry <run>`. A run checks the free disk before it starts, and the diagnoser names this kind of failure `disk`: no retry helps until space is freed.

rows.title: Failure: `nuclear-graph knowledge check` fails
rows.summary: The knowledge base is behind the working tree: a generated asset is not what the tree gives now, a hand-written row's source changed, a row is invalid, or the graph holds an older revision. Build, review, check and ingest.
body: - `stale: assets/<shelf>/<file>.json ...` → `nuclear-graph knowledge build`.
- `review: <id> was written from <source>, which changed` → read the change; update the row or `nuclear-graph knowledge review <id>`.
- `<shelf>/<id>: links to <other>, which no row has` → fix the link or add the row.
- `the graph holds revision N and the knowledge base is revision M` → `nuclear-graph ingest`.
- `<file>: no section of sections.toml claims it` → give the new document a section in `sections.toml`.

rows.title: Failure: the request names nothing the project declares
rows.summary: Which declaration is it? A change, a rename or a fix of something that exists must name it as the project declares it (`Order`, `CancelOrder`): none of the project's names is written in the request. `nuclear gen inspect` lists them.
body: **Looks like.** The analysis of a run stops with this question; no file was written.

**Cause.** The strategy of the request (`strategy:member`, `strategy:refactor-rename`, `strategy:data-migration`...) starts in the file that declares what changes, and the request names no declaration of the project: the name is misspelled, is a field or a method (only declarations are looked up), or is not in this project.
**Next step.** Write the declaration's name in the request as the project writes it, then run it again. A field or a method is renamed by hand: the compiler then names every use.

rows.title: Failure: the request lacks a fact its strategy cannot start without
rows.summary: A run stops at its analysis when the request does not say something nobody may guess: the fields of a resource, the url of an API, the two names of a rename, what should happen instead. The step lists the questions; answer them in the spec and run it again.
body: **Looks like.** `the request does not say: ...` at the Analysis step of the Specification stage; nothing was generated or written.

**Cause.** Each strategy names the facts it needs (`data.needs` of its row). The analyst looks for each one in the request (a `Key | Type` table, `name:type` pairs, an example answer, a url, `should`...) and asks for the ones it does not find. Agents never invent a field, a rule or a name.
**Next step.** Add the answer to the spec's description, then `nuclear-builder retry <run> --from spec`. The strategy is wrong for the request: name the right one in the spec (`- Strategy: usecase`).

rows.title: Failure: a local model's answer never ends (the local models are on standby)
rows.summary: Seen with the Nuclear Developer's local models, now on standby (ADR-platform-0013): no tool of NuclearLang runs a local model, so it happens only on an installation from before that decision, where a model's answer has no limit and the Developer waits for it. Stop the model and update NuclearLang (`nuclear update`): the Developer and its models are taken away.
body: **Looks like.** A chat question, an analysis or a piece with no answer after several minutes, and every later call to the Developer waiting as well; `ollama ps` shows the model loaded and working.
**Cause.** The Developer's connections gave a model its context window only, not a limit on what it writes. Seen with `qwen2.5-coder:3b` as assistant, `llama3.2:1b`, `phi3:3.8b` and `qwen2.5:1.5b`.

**Next step.** `ollama stop <model>`, then `nuclear update`: the set-up of the profile `remote` takes away the Developer's service and the models NuclearLang pulled. The work goes to an agent or an API provider.
asks: the developer hangs and nothing answers

rows.title: Failure: a local model's window is too small for the factory (Ollama, OpenCode)
rows.summary: A member worked by OpenCode on one of Ollama's models fails before it starts, or with Ollama's `the prompt is longer than the context length`: the model's window holds fewer than the 16 384 tokens an agent of the factory needs. OpenCode cannot set a window, so Ollama gives the model's own `num_ctx`, else its server's default (4 096 under 24 GiB of VRAM). Make a variant with a larger window and choose it.
body: **Looks like.** `<model> answers with a window of 4096 tokens and an agent of the factory needs at least 16384`, or `<model>'s window in Ollama is smaller than what the factory sends`, in a run's step or a chat answer.

**Cause.** An agent's first request is about 8 000 tokens (OpenCode, the role, both MCP servers' tools) and each turn adds the tools' results; `/set parameter num_ctx` in `ollama run` changes only that session.

**Next step.** `printf 'FROM <model>\nPARAMETER num_ctx 32768\n' > Modelfile && ollama create <model>-32k -f Modelfile`, then choose `ollama/<model>-32k` for the member (`nuclear-builder team member update <team> <member> --model ollama/<model>-32k`); or `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768` in Ollama's service, for every model. A model that does not fit in the GPU with it is slow: `ollama ps` says where it runs.
keys: prompt is longer than the context length
asks: the prompt is longer than the context length
